true_evaluate_items.topic: Discontinued operations presentation (ASC 205-20)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the medical device division still qualifies for discontinued operations and where to report the consumer product line sale — judgment about ASC 205-20 classification with competing stakeholder interpretations.

true_evaluate_items.topic: GAAP vs IFRS development costs
true_evaluate_items.justification: Asks candidate to recommend which reporting framework (U.S. GAAP vs IFRS) the company should adopt for its European listing — requires weighing conservatism, investor protection, and economic value representation tradeoffs.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Forecast bias detection
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating a systematic 10.7% average forecast bias pattern and recommending corrective action to the controller — must assess competing rationales (maintain vs. adjust vs. abandon quantitative model) and justify a recommendation.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Reciprocal allocation method
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires recommending a cost allocation method among three competing approaches (direct, step-down, reciprocal) with tradeoffs involving 30% mutual service levels, pricing accuracy, and cost-benefit — mature evaluate-pattern with explicit 'Recommend...' framing.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Value chain cost management
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires recommending where to focus cost reduction efforts (manufacturing at 35% vs. non-manufacturing at 65% of total product cost) — must weigh arithmetic evidence against the CEO's initial preference and make a strategic resource allocation recommendation.

true_evaluate_items.topic: JIT quality requirement
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether to implement JIT based on supplier defect rates, inventory levels, and setup times — must choose among full implementation, rejection, phased approach, or partial implementation with tradeoffs between quality prerequisites and operational targets.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Tone at the top and ethical culture
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which COSO principle is violated when a division VP overrides revenue recognition controls and the CFO dismisses it — must assess multiple competing COSO principle claims and identify the root cause control environment failure.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Risk likelihood-impact assessment prioritization
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires prioritizing four identified risks using expected monetary value vs. strategic impact — must weigh quantifiable financial exposure against threats to strategic objectives under constrained resources, a classic evaluate tradeoff.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Entity-level vs. transaction-level risk assessment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which of four entity-level risks is most critical when corporate risk assessment has historically focused on transaction-level controls — must assess control environment, IT obsolescence, regulatory change, and key-person dependency tradeoffs.

true_evaluate_items.topic: IT general controls change management
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the severity of a control deficiency in emergency patch deployment where the IT manager unilaterally tests and deploys with no documented approval or rollback plan — must assess significance and recommend appropriate remediation.

true_evaluate_items.topic: External communication — third-party control reporting
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating how to respond to a SOC 1 Type 2 control exception at an outsourced service provider — must assess whether to accept remediation, terminate contract, adjust audit approach, or request bridge letter/updated SOC report.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Monitoring frequency evaluation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the internal audit director's proposal to shift all monitoring to continuous/automated approaches — must weigh risk level, control nature, rate of change, and cost-benefit across different monitoring cadences.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Control deficiency classification
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating and classifying three control findings along the severity spectrum (deficiency/significant deficiency/material weakness) — must apply COSO Principle 17 criteria with judgment about materiality and reasonable possibility.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Audit committee oversight independence
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating audit committee composition (CEO's brother, retired ops manager, independent CPA) and recommending governance changes — must assess independence under COSO Principle 2, financial expertise requirements, and executive session practices.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Principal vs. agent (ASC 606)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether Swift Logistics is a principal or agent under ASC 606 and whether changing from commission to fixed-fee billing alters the classification — must apply control-based criteria to competing framing arguments.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Intangible classification (ASC 350/805)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the classification of five acquired items as finite-lived intangibles, indefinite-lived intangibles, or goodwill — must apply ASC 805 recognition criteria and ASC 350 subsequent measurement rules with judgment on each item.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Subsequent events (ASC 855)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating three post-balance-sheet events (bankruptcy, warehouse fire, lawsuit settlement) and determining which are Type I (adjustment) vs. Type II (disclosure) — each event requires independent judgment about whether conditions existed at year-end.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Cloud computing — SaaS migration decision
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether to migrate accounting systems to SaaS cloud platform with competing IT (40% cost savings) vs. compliance (HIPAA/GDPR concerns) analyses — must recommend a course of action addressing data residency and regulatory gaps.

true_evaluate_items.topic: ERP segregation of duties
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the most effective remediation for incompatible duties discovered during ERP post-implementation review — must assess role-based access controls, manual oversight, or system reconfiguration against audit trail adequacy claims.

true_evaluate_items.topic: ROI and residual income — capital allocation decision
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating where to place a 12% expansion project using both ROI and residual income analysis — must reconcile South's higher ROI (20%) with North's higher residual income ($150K vs $100K) and assess behavioral incentives under each metric.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 1 — tone at the top / whistleblower retaliation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the control environment is fundamentally compromised when CEO integrity messaging is contradicted by retaliatory termination of whistleblowers — must assess the gap between communicated values and operational behavior.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 15 — SOC report evaluation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether failing to implement a complementary user entity control identified in a SOC 1 Type 2 report constitutes a control deficiency — must assess severity against the assurance provided by the unmodified SOC opinion.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 7 — inherent vs. residual risk
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a risk assessment properly distinguished inherent from residual risk when an automated control had a 50-unit detection gap — must assess whether conflating control existence with control effectiveness caused the assessment failure.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 14 — internal communication
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which COSO component failure is primary when the CFO suppresses a material weakness finding from the audit committee — must distinguish between control environment, monitoring, communication, and risk assessment failures.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk response (cyber insurance gap)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the adequacy of a risk response where management accepted catastrophic cyber risk based on incomplete analysis of true financial consequences — must assess whether insurance coverage limits alone constitute adequate risk response.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Segregation of duties — vendor setup and payment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which control improvement is most effective when one employee creates vendors, enters invoices, and approves payments without adding staff — must weigh compensating control options under headcount constraint.

true_evaluate_items.topic: IT access control — terminated employee deprovisioning
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which remediation is most appropriate for preventing recurrence of terminated employee access remaining active — must assess automated deprovisioning vs. risk acceptance vs. password complexity vs. read-only conversion tradeoffs.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Application input control — sales order validation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which application control would best address sales order system errors — must choose among exception reports, reconciliation, manual approval, and real-time field validation based on effectiveness at preventing errors at entry.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk culture maturity
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether an acquired company's risk culture is mature or performative when formal governance artifacts exist but compensation incentives drive risk-concealing behavior — must assess culture as demonstrated vs. documented.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 5 — accountability
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating why a balanced scorecard accountability structure failed when metrics were communicated but safety data was manipulated and internal controls deteriorated — must identify whether the failure was design, execution, or personnel integrity.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 8 — fraud triangle assessment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the CFO's proposed response to a procurement fraud scheme adequately addresses all three fraud triangle legs — must assess whether reducing PO limits addresses only opportunity while ignoring pressure and rationalization.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 9 — fraud risk assessment resources
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a 4-person internal audit function provides sufficient resources for fraud risk assessment across 14 international plants — must assess whether outsourcing the assessment methodology (not ownership) is appropriate under COSO.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk appetite strategic alignment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a $780M investment proposal in high-geopolitical-risk country is consistent with the board's risk appetite statement — must reconcile the board's 'moderate risk' language with explicit criteria about technical expertise and operational capacity.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 3 — authority and responsibility in matrix orgs
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the root cause of a control breakdown where a regional controller deferred a write-down under dual reporting pressure — must assess whether accountability ambiguity in the matrix structure caused the failure.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 9 — risk response adequacy
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the risk committee's response to a high-likelihood/critical-impact supply chain risk is proportionate — must assess whether dual-sourcing one component and maintaining a 2-day reserve is adequate for a risk rated critical.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 3 — matrix reporting structure conflicts
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a matrix reporting structure created an authority conflict when division controllers received competing directives from division presidents and corporate controller — must assess alignment of incentives with reporting lines.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 17 — deficiency severity classification
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the CAE correctly classified four control deficiencies along the severity spectrum — must assess which finding (credential sharing, SoD, unpatched vulnerabilities, CFO override) was misclassified and why.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk response with material weaknesses
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating risk response strategies (avoid/reduce/share/accept) for two material weaknesses under capital constraints — must select a combination that balances supplier concentration risk with segregation-of-duties risk given available resources.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 4 — board independence oversight
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating board governance where the Chairman also serves as CEO — must recommend an appropriate structural response to the activist investor's demand that addresses independence without unwarranted restructuring.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 16 — monitoring frequency in high-velocity environment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether quarterly monitoring of 8.2M daily payment transactions is sufficient when fraud went undetected for months — must assess whether monitoring cadence must be calibrated to risk velocity and transaction volume.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Cybersecurity — CIA triad ransomware evaluation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which CIA triad element poses the greatest risk when both availability (encryption) and confidentiality (exfiltration of 47K patient records) are compromised — must weigh patient safety impact against HIPAA regulatory exposure.

true_evaluate_items.topic: AI/ML governance — model bias evaluation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the appropriate remediation for a loan approval ML model showing disparate impact — must assess removing proxy variables vs. accepting accuracy benchmarks vs. adjusting thresholds vs. adding features under ECOA compliance.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Direct labor efficiency variance — investigation decision
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the controller should investigate a $2,500 efficiency variance given competing explanations (learning curve vs. hiring issue) — must weigh 8.3% excess hours against management-by-exception thresholds and manager credibility.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Three Lines of Defense — external assurance reliance
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating why relying solely on an external auditor cannot substitute for missing first and third lines of defense — must assess whether a regulator (fourth line) compensates for absent control ownership and internal audit functions.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 16 — monitoring frequency vs. risk velocity
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether annual testing of automated claims system is adequate when $1.7M fraud accumulated in 11 months — must assess the proportionality principle: monitoring frequency must match risk velocity and potential loss magnitude.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 1 — code of conduct enforcement gaps
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the CEO's claim of consistent discipline is supported when a regional VP received a written warning for $120K of personal expenses while an AP clerk was terminated — must assess whether seniority-based discrepancy violates COSO Principle 1.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 8 — fraud risk pressure/incentive assessment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether Stratton adequately assessed fraud risk when its commission cliff structure (zero payout below 95% quota) created pressure — must assess whether the compensation design, not just entity-level risk assessment, required fraud-specific evaluation.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk appetite vs. strategy alignment
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a board-approved acquisition of a cybersecurity firm is consistent with stated risk appetite when the company lacks cybersecurity expertise — must reconcile the 'activities where Apex possesses technical expertise' guardrail with board approval.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 1 — tone at the top after CEO clawback
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether exercising a CEO clawback after a revenue overstatement is sufficient under COSO Principle 1 — must assess whether reactive discipline alone satisfies the principle or whether incentive structure evaluation is also required.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 12 — authorization fraud (structuring pattern)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which control failed when a purchasing manager structured eight $49,500 POs just below the $50,000 threshold — must distinguish between preventive authorization threshold failure and detective monitoring failure that missed the pattern.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 12 — IT general control deficiencies after migration
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether the CIO correctly classified post-migration control gaps as 'transition issues' — must assess whether 847 active terminated employee accounts and missing access reviews represent control design failures under COSO Principle 12.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Risk assessment granularity for emerging risks
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether Meridian's risk assessment framework classifying only 'Financial' and 'Operational' risks adequately captures new SEC climate disclosure obligations — must assess framework comprehensiveness, granularity, and emerging risk identification.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Three Lines of Defense — assurance mapping gaps
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the root cause when all three lines of defense failed simultaneously at Pacific West Bank — must assess whether the failure is a single-line failure or a systemic coordination breakdown in the assurance mapping.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 2 — board independence in related-party transactions
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a board satisfied COSO Principle 2 when all voting directors were formally independent but approved a $120M transaction with the CEO's brother's firm without competitive bidding — must assess behavioral vs. formal independence.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk culture authenticity
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether ValleyView Energy's risk culture is genuine or performative when CEO communications emphasize safety but operational incentives prioritize production throughput — must assess culture as demonstrated through behavior vs. declared through communications.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 10 — compensating control adequacy
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether manual AP supervisor review adequately compensated for a malfunctioning automated three-way match control — must assess whether the compensating control addressed the same objectives (quantity, price, goods receipt) at comparable effectiveness.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 5 — accountability in agile teams
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating why multi-factor authentication was never implemented across 12 sprints when every role (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Security Engineering) had a defensible rationale for non-responsibility — must assess structural diffusion of accountability.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 10 — segregation of duties in small entities
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether to add headcount for proper SoD or implement compensating controls at a 22-employee credit union — must assess whether full segregation is required or whether compensating controls can reduce risk to acceptable levels in resource-constrained environment.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO ERM — risk appetite recalibration after operational loss
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating how to recalibrate risk appetite after a sole-source supplier bankruptcy caused $8.7M loss against a $2M tolerance — must assess whether to increase, decrease, maintain, or eliminate risk appetite and what strategic response is warranted.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 14 — internal communication during restructuring
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether internal communication was effective when the internal audit director position was eliminated and the CFO suppressed a deficiency finding — must assess whether the controller's reporting to the CFO satisfied COSO Principle 14 requirements.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 15 — external communication of material weakness
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the appropriate timing for disclosing a material weakness discovered in May — must choose among annual 10-K, immediate 8-K, next quarterly 10-Q, or delayed disclosure after remediation and assess each under COSO and SEC requirements.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 2 — audit committee independence
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a three-member audit committee meets independence requirements when the chair is a former CFO within the cooling-off period — must apply SEC Rule 10A-3 and COSO Principle 2 independence criteria to each member.

true_evaluate_items.topic: COSO Principle 2 — board committee risk oversight structure
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether a three-committee board structure provides comprehensive risk oversight when no committee has explicit operational/cybersecurity risk responsibility — must assess whether the existing committee charters adequately cover all material risk categories.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Cybersecurity — encryption strategy and cloud migration
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating who can access unencrypted client documents when the law firm holds decryption keys but the cloud provider manages infrastructure — must assess encryption architecture, key management model, and residual access risk under attorney-client privilege.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Cloud computing — SaaS vs. on-premise for regulated industry
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether SaaS or on-premise better addresses a FDIC-regulated bank's patch management control weakness — must weigh vendor-managed patching against data control, FDIC compliance, and management-attention tradeoffs.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Data quality investigation — measurement error vs. real decline
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the most appropriate first step when customer satisfaction drops sharply but operational metrics are stable — must assess whether to act immediately on data, investigate measurement error, assume seasonality, or mandate retraining.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Automation governance — RPA bot credential risk
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating which RPA governance failure (change management, access control, or segregation of duties) has the highest remediation priority — must assess which structural control weakness enabled the damage and prioritize based on COSO Principle 11.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Full disclosure principle (ASC 235/ASC 450)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether to disclose a major customer's credit downgrade when the CFO wants to omit it due to lending relationship concerns — must weigh full disclosure requirements, materiality to a prudent investor, and ASC 450 loss contingency disclosure criteria.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Special order decision (relevant costing)
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating whether to accept a special order at $68/unit when regular price is $95 — must apply relevant costing (incremental revenue vs. incremental cost) and weigh contribution margin against concerns about precedent-setting and excess capacity utilization.

true_evaluate_items.topic: Compensating controls — small business SoD limitation
true_evaluate_items.justification: Requires evaluating the most effective incremental compensating control for a 4-person accounting department that cannot fully segregate duties — must assess mandatory vacation/job rotation against hiring, ERP purchase, or whistleblower hotline options under headcount constraint.

misclassified_items.justification: Stem asks 'Zephyr begins the month with cash of $32,800, expects receipts of $94,200, and disbursements of $101,800. It requires a $25,000 minimum balance. How much must it borrow?' — this is a straightforward cash budget calculation (end cash = $32,800 + $94,200 - $101,800 = $25,200 ≥ $25,000 → $0). Tests procedural application of the cash budget formula, not judgment or tradeoff analysis.

Stem asks 'Lakeshore Division has operating income of $200,000. Total assets are $1,000,000, current liabilities are $100,000, and the weighted-average cost of capital is 12%. The tax rate is 30%. What is the economic value added (EVA)?' — this is a direct EVA formula application: EVA = $200K×(1-0.30) - [($1,000K-$100K)×12%]. No judgment or tradeoff required; just execute the calculation.

Stem asks 'What is the purpose of this dual-rate approach?' after describing it — this tests conceptual recall of why dual-rate transfer pricing exists ('to provide incentives for both divisions by using different prices for different purposes'). The answer is a textbook definition, not a judgment or recommendation the candidate must derive.

Stem describes a control deficiency with 'reasonable possibility of resulting in a material misstatement' and asks what it should be classified as — the description is the textbook definition of a material weakness. Tests recall of the classification term, not judgment about classification.

Stem asks 'What analytical approach should be used?' to decompose a gross margin decline into price, volume, and cost effects — this is selecting the correct tool (gross margin variance analysis) from distractors clearly unrelated. Tests analytical tool identification, not evaluation of competing strategies.

Stem asks 'What internal control concept does this reflect?' after describing separation of authorization, recordkeeping, and reconciliation duties — the answer 'Segregation of duties' is a textbook definition. Tests recall of the concept name from its description.

Stem asks 'What type of control is this?' after describing locked warehouse with badge access — the answer 'A physical control that restricts access to assets' is a direct definition match. Tests classification recall, not judgment.

Stem asks 'Which one of the following controls is preventive?' and the correct answer is the system that rejects duplicates before payment. Tests identification of preventive vs. detective control types from the definition of each — a conceptual classification exercise, not an evaluative judgment.

Stem asks 'Why is independence important here?' regarding bank reconciliation performed by an independent employee — the answer explains that independence enables objective detection of errors. Tests conceptual understanding of the purpose behind a standard internal control practice.

Stem asks 'What cloud service model is this?' after describing outsourcing servers and storage while managing own applications — the answer 'Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)' is a direct definition match. Tests recall of cloud service model terminology.

Stem asks 'What data quality dimensions are being assessed?' and the stem itself lists 'correct, complete, and consistent' — the answer 'Accuracy, completeness, and consistency' restates the stem. Tests basic vocabulary recognition, zero analytical demand.

Stem asks 'What is the appropriate draw on the line of credit?' after providing May/June sales, collection percentages, beginning cash, and disbursements. The core task is computing June cash balance ($45K+$90K+$120K-$185K=$70K before minimum check). This is a procedural cash budget calculation, not a judgment call.

Stem asks 'What would be an appropriate cost driver for this pool?' for order processing costs in ABC — the answer 'Number of customer orders processed' is the textbook cause-and-effect driver. Tests conceptual understanding of ABC cost driver selection criteria.

Stem asks 'What method is this?' after describing simultaneous equations that fully recognize mutual services — the answer is the reciprocal method definition. Tests recall of service department allocation method names from their description.

Near-clone of P1-DD-048: stem asks 'What method is this?' after identical description of simultaneous equations recognizing mutual services. Same definitional recall pattern. Represents clone redundancy (DL-012 pattern).

Stem asks 'Why does Production A receive more total allocation than Production B?' under the step-down method with specific usage percentages — the answer explains the cascade effect in the step-down sequence. Tests understanding of how allocation methodology produces a counterintuitive result, which is analysis (breaking down the mechanism), not evaluation (making a judgment or recommendation).

Stem asks 'What must be assumed to compute a meaningful combined break-even point?' for multi-product CVP — the answer 'A constant sales mix' is a textbook CVP assumption. Tests recall of an assumption underlying multi-product CVP analysis.

Stem asks 'What type of control activity is this?' after describing a supervisor recounting warehouse inventory — the answer 'Independent verification, checking the accuracy of work performed by others' is a direct definition match. Tests classification recall.

Stem asks 'Which IT general control is most clearly missing?' after describing a developer making a direct production change without approval, testing, or migration — the answer is formal change management. Tests identification of a missing control from a straightforward scenario.

Stem asks 'What is this capability called?' after describing business users building their own reports from a governed data source — the answer 'Self-service business intelligence' is a textbook definition. Tests terminology recall.

Stem asks 'What is the most appropriate immediate response?' for suspected PII exfiltration — the answer 'Activate the incident response plan, contain the breach, and begin forensic investigation' follows standard NIST SP 800-61 procedure. Tests recall of standard incident response sequence, not multi-factor judgment under ambiguity.

Stem asks 'What is the primary purpose of this plan?' for a documented cybersecurity incident response plan — the answer 'To enable a timely, coordinated response that limits damage and meets any legal notification obligations' tests understanding of the purpose of an IR plan, not evaluation.

CORRUPTED ITEM — Stem, Choices, CorrectChoice, and ExplanationCorrect are all structurally empty/missing. This item is unclassifiable on cognitive merits. Requires structural repair before any cognitive level can be assessed. Listed as Understand/Remember as a placeholder pending repair.

Stem asks 'What practice does this describe?' after describing a single authoritative source of core customer and product information — the answer 'Master data management' is a textbook definition. Tests terminology recall.

Stem asks 'Prepaid insurance is classified as:' with four balance sheet category options — the answer 'Current asset' tests basic classification recall. This is a Remember-level item despite being labeled Evaluate.

Stem asks 'Incremental budgeting bases the budget on:' with four options — the answer 'Prior period actuals adjusted for changes' is a textbook definition. Tests recall of the incremental budgeting definition, zero analytical or evaluative demand.

recommendations: IMMEDIATE: Relabel 21 Understand/Remember items from Evaluate to their correct cognitive level (primarily Understand). These are definition-recall, concept-identification, or terminology questions with zero judgment or tradeoff analysis — the largest single misclassification category (21 of 26 misclassifications).

HIGH: Relabel 3 Apply-misclassified items (P1-B-024, P1B-C-143, P1-BD-090) from Evaluate to Apply. All three are straightforward calculations (cash budget borrowing, EVA, cash collection draw) requiring formula execution only.

HIGH: Relabel 2 Analyze-misclassified items (P1-CC-071, P1-DD-051) from Evaluate to Analyze. Both test understanding of analytical mechanisms (gross margin variance decomposition, step-down cascade effect) without requiring judgment or recommendation.

HIGH: Investigate and repair P1-FD-046 (Pack D, Section F). This item has no Stem, Choices, CorrectChoice, or ExplanationCorrect — structurally corrupted. Requires content authoring or archival before any cognitive classification.

MEDIUM: The 70 true Evaluate items are concentrated in Section E (internal controls — COSO principle evaluation scenarios) and Section F (technology decisions). Sections A, B, and D have far fewer genuine Evaluate items, suggesting some sections were systematically over-labeled.

MEDIUM: Packs C and D Section E items represent the highest-quality Evaluate content in the pool — detailed scenarios with multiple competing COSO assessments, specific company names, named stakeholders, and 4-choice evaluation tasks. These should be the benchmark for future Evaluate authoring.

LOW: Pack E has the lowest Evaluate-labeling accuracy (3 of 5 are genuine) — the two misclassified items are the simplest definition-recall questions in the entire pool (prepaid insurance classification, incremental budgeting definition).

LOW: Consider unifying difficulty labels with cognitive level — many Understand items labeled Evaluate also carry inflated difficulty (Moderate/Difficult instead of Easy/Moderate). Cross-reference with DL-031 (definition-match difficulty inflation).
